title: CS Quest 6.1 · Tech that changed the world
name: Tech that changed the world
summary: Students vote on eight technology dilemmas in Would You Rather (live), defend a side, and build a rope timeline of inventions with one good change and one worry for each. No game and no live warm-up today: the vote is the warm-up and the discussion is the lesson.
iCan: name technologies that changed how people live
say one way a technology changed people, and one way people changed it
materials: Invention timeline cards printable (12 cards, one per pair)
a rope or long string across the room, with clothespins or tape
paper strips for the plus and minus notes
the Would You Rather prompt sheet (printed with the plan)
doNow: Write one thing your grandparents did without a computer that you do with one.
plan: Explore: what a tradeoff is (projector script)
Timeline Walk: invention cards on the rope
Would You Rather (live): Tech choices, 8 dilemmas

do: Hold up two cards from the timeline set, the telephone and the video call. Ask who has used each. Hang them on the rope at opposite ends.

Write the word tradeoff on the board with a plus column and a minus column. Fill one row for the video call with the class: plus, you can see your cousin far away; minus, you need a device and a connection.
say: Technology is anything people invent to solve a problem. Every one of these cards changed how people live.
People change technology too: captions were added to videos because viewers asked for them.
ask: Pick any card on the rope. What did people do before it?
explore.afterAsk: Take three answers. Point out that every answer is a tradeoff: something got easier, something got lost. That is the sentence they will write at the end.
explore.bigIdea: Technology changes how people live, and people change technology right back.

play.defend: every other reveal: one student for A, one for B, thirty seconds each
play.room: start the room from the plan page with your class picked so the run lands in class history; an open room is fine when students are not signed in

steps: Each pair gets one invention card. Pairs hang it on the rope where they think it belongs in time, oldest on the left.
Pairs write two strips for their card: a plus strip (one good change) and a minus strip (one worry), and hang them under the card.
Walk the rope together for two minutes: read the plus and minus strips out loud, and move any card the class thinks is in the wrong place.

lookFors: a minus strip that is really a plus in disguise (it is too much fun): push for a real worry such as cost, safety or something lost
a pair that cannot say what people did before their invention: send them to a neighbor card for a clue
play.misconception: Kids think new technology is simply better than old; the point of the lesson is that every technology is a tradeoff: it makes something easier and changes or loses something else.
earlyFinishers: add a second plus and minus strip to a neighbor's card
put an invention nobody brought on the rope and say where it goes in time

discuss: Which invention on the rope would you un-invent for a week? What would be better, and what would be worse?
Which vote surprised you most? Why do you think the class split that way?
showMe: Show the class split for the dilemma with the closest vote on the projector; two students say one sentence each for their side.

exit.sentencePrompt: Pick one invention from today. How did it change what people do?

rubric.line: Tech changes: a technology and how it changed people
levels: Names a technology and says one way it changed what people do
Also says how people changed the technology, or names a tradeoff

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: a frame on the board for the strips: Before this, people ___; now people ___
pairs who find defending hard get the printed prompt and thirty seconds to plan together first
the host reads each dilemma out loud before the timer starts
stretch: influenced by culture: ask why emoji exist and who decided what they look like
put a date guess on your card and check it against the answer card at the end

unpluggedTwin.title: Corners vote
materials: the printed dilemma sheet (the 8 dilemmas of the live run)
a sign for corner A and a sign for corner B
the invention timeline cards, the rope and the paper strips
steps: Read a dilemma out loud. Students walk to corner A or corner B. Count hands out loud and write the split on the board.
After every other dilemma, one student from each corner has thirty seconds to defend their side; nobody changes corners until both have spoken.
Finish with the Timeline Walk as in the plan: the rope, the cards, the plus and minus strips.

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: write one thing your grandparents did without a computer that you do with one.

Run the Corners vote with the printed dilemma sheet (walk to corner A or B, count hands, two defenders every other round), then the Timeline Walk: each pair hangs its invention card on the rope with a plus strip and a minus strip. No projector and no login needed.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

table: Explore: tradeoff, one row on the board
shortPeriod40.discuss: Which invention on the rope would you un-invent for a week? What would be better, and what would be worse?
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut; shorten the walk along the rope, not the strips

add: host 10 dilemmas instead of 8 (the plan page's block-day starter) with defenders on every reveal
the full Timeline Walk with a date guess on every card
10 minutes of the Unit 6 pre-test: the unit opener and review items on the projector

notes: No live warm-up today on purpose: the vote is the warm-up. The warm-up of 6.2 opens with this unit's opener item.
Start the room from the plan page with your class picked so the run lands in class history; an open room is fine when students are not signed in, and the step is then completed by participation.
The timer is 20 seconds a dilemma; the defenders make it a discussion, so keep them to thirty seconds each and alternate which side goes first.
The telephone, video calls and captions all appear in the exit items: use those words during the walk.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: Write one thing your grandparents did without a computer that you do with one.

Big idea: Technology changes how people live, and people change technology right back.

Timeline Walk: hang your invention card on the rope where it belongs in time. Under it, hang a plus strip (one good change) and a minus strip (one worry).

We will talk about:
- Which invention would you un-invent for a week? What would be better, and what would be worse?
- Which vote surprised you most?

steps.title: Would You Rather (live)
steps.body: Eight dilemmas about technology. Vote, then look at how the class split. When your teacher picks you, defend your side for thirty seconds.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about technology that changed the world.

steps.title: In your own words
steps.body:
Pick one invention from today. How did it change what people do?
Frame: ___ changed how people ___.
